newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ITALIAN FLAVOUR SOURS IN ENGLAND AND SCOTLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN FLAVOUR SOURS IN ENGLAND AND SCOTLAND.

text.p: British soccer's Italian flavour has soured just weeks before the English premier league and Scottish season kick off, with players falling foul of coaches and clubs falling short of their demands.
English premier league side Derby are the latest side likely to miss out on a big-name Italian signing, the club admitting on Wednesday they had all but given up on luring Roberto Baggio.
Baggio, once the world's most expensive player, said last month he wanted to leave five-times European champions AC Milan before the start of the season.
"It's more doubtful," said a Derby spokesman. "It is more likely to be no than yes."
Italian newspapers have linked Baggio to several clubs including Vicenza, Napoli, Sampdoria and Spain's Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.
Derby were reportedly prepared to pay 10 million pounds ($17 million) for the 30-year-old striker.
The transfer market has come to life in recent weeks as English clubs frantically try to complete deals before the August 9 start to the season. The Scotland season kicks off on August 2.

Scottish giants Celtic, meanwhile, have warned Paolo Di Canio that they will make sure that if he does not play for them he will not play for anyone else either for another three years after the Italian declared he had played his last game for the club.
Di Canio, formerly of Juventus and Napoli, has refused to join Celtic on their pre-season tour of the Netherlands.
Celtic general manager Jock Brown said the striker is contracted to the club until 2000 and he vowed the club would not transfer him.
Another Italian international, Gianluca Vialli has also been unhappy after spending much of last season on the bench at London club Chelsea.
The striker has been linked with Celtic, along with Inter Milan's Swiss midfielder Ciri Sforza, but the club have refused to comment on the media reports.
Liverpool manager Roy Evans has harboured an interest in Middlesbrough's unsettled Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli, according to newspaper reports.
Middlesbrough, who were relegated to the English first division last season, on Tuesday transferred Brazil international Juninho to Atletico Madrid for 12 million pounds ($20.2 million).

Newcastle, unperturbed by the fickle nature of some of the Italians playing in Britain, have approached Inter Milan about signing full-back Alessandro Pistone. And Tottenham have not been put off either, making a 3.5 million pounds ($6.0 million) bid for 26-year-old Italian midfielder Federico Giunti.
Liverpool, meanwhile, were poised to sign England midfielder Paul Ince from Inter Milan for 4.2 million pounds ($7.0 million) within the next 24 hours.
The Merseysiders have already signed 20-year-old Crewe midfielder Danny Murphy in a deal estimated to be worth three million pounds.

Frenchman David Ginola, who spent much of this year on the bench at Newcastle, has held talks with Tottenham and was ready to sign for 2.5 million pounds ($4.2 million), English newspapers said on Wednesday.
Ginola had previously held talks with Greek club Olympiakos.

Derby have also confirmed that a number of clubs had expressed interest in their striker Dean Sturridge, but that none of them were prepared to pay the club's asking price of 7.0 million pounds ($11.8 million).
"There are one or two interested, but not at the price," said the club spokesman. "No-one has come back to us yet."
Tottenham, Leeds, Arsenal and Middlesbrough have indicated an interest, with bids of up to five million pounds ($8.4 million).
